identification: Box of 6 to 8 pieces of 18th century English blue and white and polychrome porcelain, some damaged. Google Lens on photo 3 matches the fluted teapot (blue shoulder with gilt 'cracked ice', flower sprays) to Philip Christian & Co of Liverpool c.1770 rather than Worcester; a dealer (Moorabool Antique Galleries) has a similar one at A$1,450 asking (seen in Lens results only, page not opened).

searches_tried: comps.py (pipeline and work) for worcester porcelain, worcester teapot, 18th century porcelain: no same-item hits. Gowans API for worcester, teapot, caughley, lowestoft, etc: only Royal Worcester and modern lots. WebSearch x5 (scale blue teapot, crescent teabowl, strainer dish, sauceboat, damaged Worcester lots Australia). Bonhams and Carters blocked (403/429). No sold price found for a scale blue fluted polychrome Worcester teapot; asking prices for dealer scale blue teapots seen in snippets run well into the hundreds to low thousands but are not recorded as entries. Rates assumed GBP 2.05, CAD 1.1. eBay sold would help settle it. | chrome: Terapeak UK sold 'worcester scale blue teapot' (only copies and later pieces, under A$85); LiveAuctioneers price results 'worcester scale blue teapot' (newest same-type result is Feb 2024 at GBP 240 for a 10-piece collection, older than 24 months, not used); Terapeak UK sold 2 years 'first period worcester'. Real First Period Worcester teapots sold for about A$360 to A$370 on eBay UK; damaged tea bowls and dishes A$15 to A$190.
chrome_hint: eBay sold: 'Worcester scale blue teapot 18th century' and 'Worcester fluted teabowl crescent mark' (Sold items); also LiveAuctioneers/Invaluable results for 'Worcester scale blue teapot fluted' and the-saleroom Worcester price guide.
viewing_check: Turn the scale blue teapot over: a blue square seal or crescent mark and a greenish glow when held to light suggest real Worcester; a Samson copy is greyer and harder. Check spout, handle and lid for chips or restoration. Count the damaged pieces.
